newsitem.title: USA: Runner to cross U.S. in support of volunteer summit.
newsitem.headline: Runner to cross U.S. in support of volunteer summit.

text.p: In one of the more enthusiastic demonstrations of support for a national "summit" on volunteerism, a Cambodian refugee is planning to run across the United States to encourage Americans to join summit goals.
"It's my appreciation to America," Hoang Taing told Reuters on Tuesday before setting off from Philadelphia's Liberty Bell on her 3,000 mile (4,828 km) run.
"When I was a refugee and I did not speak any English, I came to America and America helped me so much," she said.

Hoang Taing said she did not know her age, due to disruptions caused in her homeland by the ultra-radical Khmer Rouge, whose "killing fields" regime between 1975-78 saw the deaths of more than one million Cambodians.
The run will take about 120 days.
It is sponsored by the United Way, with assistance from the University of California, United Airlines and others, she said.
